cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/ResourceManager.as:41,186,200-214; verified by decrypting reference/extracted/android/115_Mobile_SHS3Resource.bin at key 104 -> valid CWS v17 SWF, 1,040,849 bytes inflated, 1,912 SymbolClass entries
lane_impact: Cross-lane extraction rule (art, audio, items): keys are 104/117/111/109/103 by resource, derived not guessed - anyone opening the remaining blobs can stop brute-forcing.
quote: ResourceManager.as:41 `internal static var resourceFileNameArray:Array = ["shs3resource.swf","musicresource.swf","soundresource.swf","imageresource.swf","bgresource.swf"];` :186 `ba = decryptByteArray(ba,resourceFileNameArray[num].charCodeAt(1));` :205 `for(var i:int = 3; i < 256; i++)` :207 `if(i % 11 == 0)` :213 `ba[i] ^= key;`
text: The XOR key for the five obfuscated Android resource blobs is NOT one constant - it is the SECOND CHARACTER of the resource's filename, so every blob has its own key. ResourceManager.as:186 passes 'resourceFileNameArray[num].charCodeAt(1)' into decryptByteArray, and :41 lists the five filenames. That yields shs3resource.swf -> 'h' = 104, musicresource.swf -> 'u' = 117, soundresource.swf -> 'o' = 111, imageresource.swf -> 'm' = 109, bgresource.swf -> 'g' = 103. This reconciles the two keys the Stage-0 brief already carries (C1's 109 from Mobile.as:352 and C3's 111 for the sound blob) and predicts the other three. Also note decryptByteArray only touches bytes 3..255 (swapping every i%11==0 byte with i+256), which is why the files still begin with a readable 'CWS' magic.
